issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a public Farm.singFarmSong() method (used to play the Old MacDonald song), but the solution implementation provides a method named playFarmSong() instead of singFarmSong(). This name/signature mismatch between template/problem and solution is structural and can confuse students who compare their work to the solution or follow the template's method name. It also means the template's singFarmSong() contract is not satisfied by the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem and template by renaming playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() method that delegates to playFarmSong(). This ensures the method name and signature match across problem, template, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a public method named singFarmSong() on Farm, but the solution implements a public method named playFarmSong() instead. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement (implement singFarmSong) to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's public method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() (or conversely, update the problem statement and template to use playFarmSong()) so that the public method name is consistent across problem, template, and solution. Ensure the method signature and behavior remain the same.
